answer: To suppress Sybil attacks among sensory agents deployed along a rock ledge, the system requires distance-bounding challenges. Each agent must echo random nonces across local radio links while a timing kernel measures time-of-flight. An attacker attempting to register fake identities incurs the verifiable expense of procuring and placing distinct physical transceivers at unique coordinates. However, RF multipath reflections can skew delay calculations, mistakenly rejecting valid agents.
